evidence:
tests/test_native_expiry.py:222 `def test_a_death_mid_expiry_completes_the_same_expiry(self):` ... :237-241 `done = self.reclaim(copy, "--recorded", expect=None)
                if done.returncode != EXIT.OK:
                    done = self.reclaim(copy)
                self.assertEqual(done.returncode, EXIT.OK, ...)`
fix: Split by cut. Before `replaced`, require `--recorded` to exit OK. From `replaced` on, require the specific 'nothing left' outcome. Never fall back to an unrecorded reclaim inside this test.
reviewer: tests/test_native_expiry.py:237-241: when --recorded returns anything other than OK, the test falls back to a plain reclaim, so at the created/written/staged-durable cuts a refused, uncertain or faulting --recorded is masked. purge 30 expires the same p0/p1 at a fresh instant, so the 'same expiry' property is never distinguished. Partial coverage elsewhere: recorded_base plus test_a_recorded_reclaim_installs... (:277) requires --recorded to install after the 'created' cut on a serving node.
scenario: `store reclaim --recorded` regresses at the created/written/staged-durable cuts, before the install, where the comment says it must complete the recorded instant. It refuses, or exits 3 (uncertain), or faults. The test then runs a plain `store reclaim`, which picks a new instant, reclaims p0/p1, and passes. Uncertain and refused are both silently replaced by a retry, and the 'same expiry' property is never checked.
title: The test of resuming the recorded expiry falls back to a fresh reclaim, so a broken --recorded still passes
